chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from the one who mentioned it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When a man kills two men or more than that, he shall be killed by them (the guardians of the deceased).

key_terms.الرجلين: Two men (dual form) — specifying the minimum threshold for the ruling on multiple homicide
key_terms.قتل: Killing, homicide (qatl) — the unlawful taking of a life, subject to Islamic penal law
key_terms.قُتِلَ بِهِمْ: He shall be killed by them — the passive indicates state-sanctioned execution at the initiative of the victims' guardians (awliya' al-dam)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling when someone kills two or more people?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a ruling on qisas (retaliation) in cases of multiple homicide: when a person kills two or more victims, he is subject to execution at the hands of the heirs/guardians of the slain. This ruling affirms that multiple victims' rights do not cancel each other out — each victim's family retains the right to qisas. The Imam's audience would have understood 'بهم' (by them) to mean the collective right of all victims' guardians to demand and carry out the prescribed punishment.
